states.name: Alabama
states.boardName: Alabama Board of Medical Examiners & Medical Licensure Commission
states.renewalAnchor: Fixed date: all licenses expire annually on December 31, regardless of when issued. Renewal window is October 1 through December 31 via the Licensee Gateway.
states.cmeDetails: 25 hours per year. at least 25 Category 1, 2 hrs controlled substances, required topics: Ethics.
states.cmeSource: Ala. Admin. Code r. 540-X-14-.02; r. 540-X-4-.09(8) (controlled substance CME)
states.renewalFee: $300 (full MD/DO license, annual renewal). ACSC (Alabama Controlled Substances Certificate) renewal is a separate $150 if held.
states.lateFee: $100, applied to renewals submitted January 1 through January 31 (Ala. Admin. Code r. 545-X-2-.03; also stated in the Board's Medical Digest, Fall 2020)
states.graceOrLapse: Grace period January 1-31 for full MD/DO licenses only, with the $100 late fee; the license remains in Active status (authorized to practice) until midnight January 31. If not renewed within 31 days after due, the license automatically becomes Inactive (r. 545-X-2-.03(6)). Reinstatement requires a paper application to the Medical Licensure Commission with all past-due renewal fees (up to two years) plus $250 (per r. 545-X-2-.03(7); the Board's reinstatement letter states $550 if expired at the most recent Dec. 31, $850 if expired earlier), a $65 criminal background check with two FBI fingerprint cards, 25 AMA PRA Category 1 CME credits earned in the previous 12 months, and proof of citizenship/lawful presence. Physicians inactive two or more years must enter a reentry agreement with the Board. Incomplete reinstatement applications expire six months from receipt. The ACSC has NO grace period; it expires December 31 and requires reissue if lapsed.
steps: Complete your CME for the cycle (25 hours) (see details below)
Log in to the Alabama Board of Medical Examiners & Medical Licensure Commission renewal portal
Complete the renewal application and answer the attestation questions
Pay the renewal fee ($300 (full MD/DO license, annual renewal))
Submit and save your confirmation
pitfalls: The ACSC (state controlled substances certificate) has no grace period: it expires December 31 and you may not prescribe controlled substances after that date even though the medical license itself stays Active through January 31. Lapsed ACSCs go through a separate reissue process.

Licenses obtained through the Interstate Medical Licensure Compact must be renewed on the IMLC renewal website, not through Alabama's Licensee Gateway; an ACSC held alongside an IMLC license still renews with the Alabama board.

Miss January 31 and the license automatically becomes Inactive by rule; reinstatement is a paper application with FBI fingerprint cards, a $65 background check, 25 Category 1 CME credits from the prior 12 months, and a prorated fee the board quotes at $550-$850 depending on when the license expired. Two or more years inactive adds a mandatory reentry agreement with the Board.

The 25 Category 1 CME credits must be earned during the calendar year of renewal, and the board requires licensees to complete the renewal application personally and attest to its accuracy; delegating it to office staff violates the attestation.

Foreign-national licensees must submit a Declaration of Lawful Presence with documentation and have it approved before the renewal application becomes available in the Gateway, so starting in late December leaves no processing margin.

faqs.question: When does my Alabama medical license expire and when can I renew?
faqs.answer: Every MD/DO license expires December 31 each year, regardless of issue date. The renewal window opens October 1 in the Licensee Gateway (dashboard.albme.gov) and runs through December 31. Reminder emails go to your address of record starting in October.

faqs.question: What does renewal cost?
faqs.answer: $300 for the full license. If you hold an Alabama Controlled Substances Certificate, its renewal is a separate $150. Pain management registration, if held, is another $100.

faqs.question: What happens if I miss December 31?
faqs.answer: Full MD/DO licenses get a grace period from January 1 to January 31 with a $100 late fee, and the license stays in Active status until midnight January 31. The ACSC gets no grace period: you cannot write controlled substances after December 31 until it is reissued.

faqs.question: What if I miss the January 31 grace deadline?
faqs.answer: The license automatically becomes Inactive under Ala. Admin. Code r. 545-X-2-.03(6). Reinstatement requires a written application with past-due renewal fees (up to two years) plus $250, per the rule; the board's reinstatement letter quotes $550 if the license expired at the most recent December 31 and $850 if earlier, plus a $65 criminal background check with two FBI fingerprint cards, 25 Category 1 CME credits from the previous 12 months, and proof of citizenship. Inactive two or more years also requires a reentry agreement with the Board.

faqs.question: How much CME do I need to renew?
faqs.answer: 25 AMA PRA Category 1 Credits or equivalent earned during the calendar year. ACSC holders also attest to the biennial 2-hour controlled substance prescribing CME. A one-time board-designated professional boundaries course is required (existing licensees by 12/31/2025; new licensees within 12 months of licensure).

faqs.question: I got my Alabama license through the IMLC. Do I renew it the same way?
faqs.answer: No. Licenses obtained via the Interstate Medical Licensure Compact must be renewed through the IMLC renewal website, not the Alabama Licensee Gateway. If you also hold an ACSC, renew the license via IMLC first, then the ACSC with the Alabama board.

states.name: Alaska
states.boardName: Alaska State Medical Board (Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing, Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development)
states.renewalAnchor: All medical licenses expire December 31 of even-numbered years, regardless of issuance date. Current cycle: January 1, 2025 through December 31, 2026. Licenses issued within 90 days of the expiration date are issued to the next biennial expiration date. One renewal notice is sent by email or mail at least 30 days before expiration, usually in late October.
states.cmeDetails: 50 hours per 2-year cycle. at least 50 Category 1, 2 hrs opioid prescribing.
states.renewalFee: $350 (active MD or DO, full-term biennial renewal, or lapsed less than 1 year). $175 prorated if the license was first issued in the second year of the cycle. Inactive status: $200 full-term or $100 prorated. Retired status: $150 one time.
states.lateFee: None published. Alaska has no separate late-renewal penalty fee; a physician lapsed less than 1 year pays the same $350 biennial renewal fee but must add FSMB clearance if lapsed at least 60 days. The real penalty is the lapse itself, since there is no grace period.
states.graceOrLapse: No grace period. The license lapses after December 31 and it is illegal to practice with a lapsed license from day one. Lapsed at least 60 days but under 1 year: renewal application, $350 fee, CME proof, plus clearance from FSMB sent directly to the division (12 AAC 40.025(a)). Lapsed 1 to 5 years: Reinstatement of Medical License Application (form 08-4974), CME proof, FSMB clearance, DEA clearance sent directly by DEA, license verifications from every state ever licensed, and hospital privilege verifications for the past 5 years (12 AAC 40.025(b)). Lapsed 5 years or more: considered expired and may not be reinstated; a new license application is required. A separate 30-day grace period can be requested on the renewal form solely for completing unfinished CME.
states.processingTime: 4 to 6 weeks for a correct and complete renewal application (per form 08-0077); once processed, the license is printable via the MY LICENSE portal
steps: Complete your CME for the cycle (50 hours) (see details below)
Log in to the Alaska State Medical Board (Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing, Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development) renewal portal
Complete the renewal application and answer the attestation questions
Pay the renewal fee ($350 (active MD or DO, full-term biennial renewal, or lapsed less than 1 year))
Submit and save your confirmation
pitfalls: There is no grace period. Form 08-0077 states in bold that the license lapses after December 31 and it is illegal to work on a lapsed license. Alaska sends only one renewal notice, usually in late October, and failure to receive it does not excuse late renewal.

Lapsing is expensive in paperwork even if brief: at 60 days lapsed you must obtain FSMB clearance sent directly to the division; at 1 year you need the full reinstatement application (08-4974) with DEA clearance and verifications from every state where you have ever been licensed; at 5 years the license is dead and you start over as a new applicant.

DEA holders must complete the PDMP sections of the renewal: log in to the AWARxE account (alaska.pmpaware.net), verify specialty, contact info, DEA number, and every delegate, and attest to the review requirements. The renewal cannot move forward without PDMP account verification.

Only CME hours actually awarded inside the two-year window (January 1 of the odd year through December 31 of the even year) count toward that renewal; hours do not roll over. The division runs computer-generated random audits after renewal, and you must keep CME documentation for at least 4 years (12 AAC 02.960). PARS/CME Passport reporting is optional but lets board staff verify your hours without you submitting certificates.

Paper renewals cannot be faxed or emailed (credit card data is not accepted by email); mail to PO Box 110806, Juneau. Online renewal through MY LICENSE requires a myAlaska account and a web authorization code sent to the email on file, so update your email of record before renewal season.
A US Social Security Number must be on file before the license can be renewed (AS 08.01.100); foreign citizens without one must file the exemption request form 08-4372.

faqs.question: When does my Alaska medical license expire?
faqs.answer: December 31 of even-numbered years, for every licensee regardless of when the license was issued. The current cycle runs January 1, 2025 through December 31, 2026, so the next renewal deadline is December 31, 2026. Exception: a license first issued within 90 days of the expiration date (after roughly October 1 of the even year) is issued straight through to the next biennial expiration.

faqs.question: How much does renewal cost?
faqs.answer: $350 for a full-term active biennial renewal (MD and DO use the same form and fee). If your license was first issued in the second year of the cycle, the renewal fee is prorated to $175. Inactive status renewal is $200 (or $100 prorated), and converting to retired status is a one-time $150.

faqs.question: Can I renew online?
faqs.answer: Yes. Renew through the MY LICENSE self-service portal at ProfessionalLicense.Alaska.Gov/MYLICENSE, which signs in through your myAlaska account. Paper renewal (form 08-0077) is also accepted by mail only; faxed or emailed applications are not accepted.

faqs.question: Is there a grace period if I miss the deadline?
faqs.answer: No. The license lapses after December 31 and practicing on a lapsed license is illegal. If lapsed under 1 year you renew with the normal $350 fee plus FSMB clearance (required once lapsed at least 60 days); lapsed 1 to 5 years requires the full reinstatement application with DEA clearance and state verifications; lapsed 5 or more years cannot be reinstated at all. The only grace mechanism is a 30-day extension you can request on the form specifically to finish CME.

faqs.question: What do I attest to for CME?
faqs.answer: 50 hours of AMA Category 1 (or AOA Category 1 or 2) CME awarded between January 1 of the odd year and December 31 of the even year, averaging 25 per year, including at least 2 hours in pain management and opioid use and addiction unless you certify you hold no DEA registration. Retired-status renewals are exempt. The division audits a random percentage after renewal; keep records 4 years, or use ACCME PARS so staff can verify hours for you.

faqs.question: How long does renewal processing take?
faqs.answer: Plan on 4 to 6 weeks for a correct and complete application. Once processed, the license is available for printing through the MY LICENSE portal.

faqs.question: I hold a DEA registration. What extra steps apply?
faqs.answer: You must be registered with the Alaska PDMP, and the renewal requires verifying your PDMP account at alaska.pmpaware.net: confirming your specialty, contact information, DEA number, and delegates, and acknowledging the requirement to review a patient's prescription history before prescribing, administering, or dispensing federally scheduled II or III controlled substances (and every 30 days for up to 90 days, then quarterly for ongoing treatment). Practitioners who directly dispense scheduled II to IV substances must report dispensations daily.

states.name: Arizona
states.boardName: Arizona Medical Board
states.doBoardName: Arizona Board of Osteopathic Examiners in Medicine and Surgery
states.renewalCycle: Biennial (2 years) for both MD and DO
states.renewalAnchor: MD: every other year on or before the licensee's birthday (A.R.S. 32-1430(A); the on-year depends on your license record, check your profile at azmd.gov Doctor Search). DO: December 31 of either even-numbered or odd-numbered years depending on the licensee's assigned renew-by date; the DO renewal portal opens on or about October 1.
states.cmeDetails: MD: 40 hours per 2-year cycle. 3 hrs opioid prescribing. DO: 40 hours per 2-year cycle. at least 24 Category 1, 3 hrs opioid prescribing.
states.renewalFee: $500 (MD active license, 2-year renewal). DO: $636 biennial, non-refundable.
states.lateFee: MD: $350 penalty in addition to the $500 fee if renewed more than 30 days after the birthday due date ($850 total on the paper form). DO: $175 late fee in addition to the $636 fee if renewing January 31 through April 30 ($811 total).
states.graceOrLapse: MD: renewal within 30 days after the birthday incurs no penalty; from 31 days to 4 months after the birthday you renew with the $350 penalty; the license automatically expires 4 months after the birthday and an expired MD must reapply for licensure (A.R.S. 32-1430(A) and (D)); practicing on an expired license violates the Medical Practice Act. DO: renew by midnight December 31; renewals through January 31 incur no penalty; February 1 through April 30 requires the $175 late fee; the license expires May 1 and the board states there is no reinstatement of an expired DO license, you must reapply as a new physician, which the board says can take up to 6 months with no guarantee of relicensure.
states.processingTime: MD paper renewals: allow 4-6 weeks (board form instructions); MD online renewals generate an email confirmation when approved, no published timeline. DO online renewal updates the public profile within minutes unless disclosures or status changes require staff review.
steps: Complete your CME for the cycle (40 hours) (see details below)
Log in to the Arizona Medical Board renewal portal
Complete the renewal application and answer the attestation questions
Pay the renewal fee ($500 (MD active license, 2-year renewal))
Submit and save your confirmation
pitfalls: MD and DO run on completely different clocks in Arizona. MDs renew on or before their birthday every other year; DOs renew by December 31 of their assigned even or odd year. A dual-boarded practice manager who assumes one deadline will miss the other.

An expired Arizona DO license has no reinstatement path at all. After May 1 the board requires a full new-physician application, quotes up to 6 months to process, and states there is no guarantee of relicensure. The MD board likewise requires reapplication once the license auto-expires 4 months after the birthday.

DO renewal is online only: no paper form exists, checks are not accepted, and credit card payments are not taken by phone. The DO portal takes Visa, MasterCard and Discover; the MD online renewal takes Visa, MasterCard and AMEX (no Discover). Bring the right card for the right board.

Any Arizona MD with a DEA registration (or intending to get one) must register with the Controlled Substances Prescription Monitoring Program (CSPMP) under A.R.S. 36-2606; the board warns failure to register may result in Board action.

DO licensees should enter all CME in the Licensee Portal before starting the renewal, and a dual-purpose course (AOA 1-A plus opioid CME) must be entered twice, once under each requirement. DO CME waiver and extension requests are only accepted October 1 through January 30, with an approved extension giving until April 30.

faqs.question: When is my Arizona MD license renewal due?
faqs.answer: Every other year on or before your birthday (A.R.S. 32-1430(A)). You can renew up to 30 days after your birthday without penalty; after that a $350 late penalty applies, and the license automatically expires 4 months after your birthday.

faqs.question: How much does renewal cost?
faqs.answer: MD: $500 for the 2-year renewal, plus a $350 penalty if postmarked 31 or more days after the due date. DO: $636 biennial, plus a $175 late fee if renewing January 31 through April 30; all DO fees are non-refundable.

faqs.question: What happens if I let my license lapse?
faqs.answer: MD: the license automatically expires 4 months after your birthday and you must reapply for licensure; practicing after expiration violates the Medical Practice Act. DO: the license expires May 1 with no reinstatement; you must reapply as a new physician, which the board says can take up to 6 months with no guarantee of relicensure.

faqs.question: Can I renew on paper?
faqs.answer: MD: yes, the board publishes an MD Paper Renewal form and asks you to allow 4-6 weeks for processing, though online renewal is preferred. DO: no, the process is entirely online through the Thentia licensee portal and the board will not process mailed checks.

faqs.question: Do I need to submit CME certificates with my renewal?
faqs.answer: Only if selected for audit. MDs attest to 40 hours per cycle and submit the CME Audit Form with proof (including the 3 hours of opioid prescribing CME) only when audited. DOs attest and are also subject to random audit; the DO board holds the physician responsible for recordkeeping and lets you log CME in the Licensee Portal.

faqs.question: When does the DO renewal window open?
faqs.answer: The DO renewal portal opens on or about October 1 of the renewal year, and renewal notices are mailed the last Friday in October. Renew by December 31 to avoid issues; January 1-31 is a no-penalty grace period.

states.name: Arkansas
states.boardName: Arkansas State Medical Board
states.renewalCycle: Annual (1 year); an optional 2-year multiyear registration is available on request under A.C.A. 17-95-414 with 2 years of fees and equivalent CME
states.renewalAnchor: Annually on or before the last day of the licensee's birth month. Board language: "Your medical license, if granted, must be renewed annually on or before the last day of your birth month. There is no grace period." Email reminders go out about 60, 45, and 30 days before the end of the birth month; failure to receive notice is not an excuse.
states.cmeDetails: 20 hours per year. at least 10 Category 1, 1 hrs opioid prescribing, 3 hrs controlled substances.
states.renewalFee: $11 (MD/DO annual renewal, per the ASMB fee schedule PDF reflecting the Act 114 of 2023 fee reduction stated to run 7/1/2023 through 6/30/2026). Statutory default is $70 per year under A.C.A. 17-95-411(a)(4), which is the cap; the board may keep fees reduced in future years but the schedule says fees are subject to change without notice. Waived for active-duty military.
states.lateFee: $50 late fee to reinstate an expired MD/DO license (fee schedule and MD application packet agree)
states.graceOrLapse: No grace period. Failure to renew before midnight on the last day of the birth month causes the license to automatically expire, and practicing on a lapsed license is illegal. Reinstatement requires the renewal plus the $50 late fee. If the license has lapsed 5 or more consecutive years, the physician must reapply completely as a new applicant (the board may reuse some original file verifications but does not guarantee it); A.C.A. 17-1-107 requires reduced reinstatement requirements for previously licensed practitioners in good standing.
steps: Complete your CME for the cycle (20 hours) (see details below)
Log in to the Arkansas State Medical Board renewal portal
Complete the renewal application and answer the attestation questions
Pay the renewal fee ($11 (MD/DO annual renewal, per the ASMB fee schedule PDF reflecting the Act 114 of 2023 fee reduction stated to run 7/1/2023 through 6/30/2026))
Submit and save your confirmation
pitfalls: There is no grace period at all: the license auto-expires at midnight on the last day of your birth month, a $50 late fee applies to reinstate, and practicing on the lapsed license in the interim is illegal (MD application packet, Rev 4/15/2026).

Renewal reminders come only by email to the private email address on file, and the board states that failure to receive notice is NOT an excuse for nonrenewal, so a stale email address can silently cost you your license.

The CME compliance window is birth month to birth month, not the calendar year: 20 hours annually measured from the birth month of the previous year through the birth month of the current year, 50% Category 1 in your primary practice area, plus 1 of the 20 hours in prescribing opioids and/or benzodiazepines (board FAQ, Rule 17).

The posted $11 renewal fee is a temporary reduction under Act 114 of 2023 that the fee schedule says ends June 30, 2026 and may or may not continue; the statutory fee is $70 per year (A.C.A. 17-95-411), so verify the amount at checkout rather than budgeting from the old schedule.
A license lapsed for 5 or more consecutive years cannot simply be reinstated: the board requires a complete new application as if applying for the first time.
The board's web domain moved from armedicalboard.org to armedicalboard.adh.arkansas.gov; old bookmarks redirect today, but use the arkansas.gov address for the login portal.

faqs.question: When is my Arkansas medical license renewal due?
faqs.answer: Annually, on or before the last day of your birth month. Renewal is done online through the board's licensee portal. The board emails reminders roughly 60, 45, and 30 days before the end of your birth month, but not receiving a notice is not an accepted excuse.

faqs.question: Is there a grace period if I miss the deadline?
faqs.answer: No. The board states explicitly that there is no grace period. The license automatically expires at midnight on the last day of your birth month, and reinstating it requires the renewal plus a $50 late fee. It is illegal to practice on the lapsed license in the meantime.

faqs.question: How much does renewal cost?
faqs.answer: The posted fee schedule lists $11 for MD/DO annual renewal, a reduced amount under Act 114 of 2023 stated to be in effect 7/1/2023 through 6/30/2026. The statutory annual fee under A.C.A. 17-95-411 is $70, which is also the cap; the fee is waived for active-duty military members.

faqs.question: Can I renew for more than one year at a time?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under A.C.A. 17-95-414 the board must offer a multiyear option: after initial licensure you may request a 2-year license or registration by submitting the required information, CME proof equivalent to the period, and 2 years of fees.

faqs.question: What CME do I need to attest at renewal?
faqs.answer: 20 hours annually, counted from the birth month of the previous year through the birth month of the current year. Half must be AMA Category 1 in your primary area of practice, and 1 of the 20 hours must cover prescribing opioids and/or benzodiazepines (Rule 17; board FAQ).

faqs.question: My license lapsed years ago. Can I reinstate it?
faqs.answer: If it has been lapsed 5 or more consecutive years, you must reapply completely as if you were a new applicant; the board may reuse some verifications from your original file but does not guarantee it. Shorter lapses are reinstated by paying the renewal and the $50 late fee. A.C.A. 17-1-107 also requires reduced reinstatement requirements for previously licensed practitioners who were in good standing.

DO: biennial cycle renewed through BreEZe; OMBC's loaded pages state the two-year period runs between the prior and current expiration dates but do not explicitly publish the anchor rule (issuance month vs other), so that detail is left unstated rather than guessed.

Submit and save your confirmation

faqs.question: Where do I actually renew?
faqs.answer: Both boards renew online through the DCA BreEZe portal at https://www.breeze.ca.gov/ (login page: /datamart/loginCADCA.do). BreEZe lets you renew once your license is within 180 days of expiration, or if it expired less than five years ago. OMBC also accepts a downloadable paper renewal form mailed with a check to 1300 National Drive, Suite 150, Sacramento, CA 95834.

faqs.question: When will I be notified that renewal is due?
faqs.answer: MBC sends email notifications starting 180 days before your expiration date directing you to renew online. Do not wait for a paper reminder.

faqs.question: What do I have to attest to during an MD renewal?
faqs.answer: The BreEZe renewal includes the mandatory Physician Survey, a Financial Interest Statement, disciplinary action and conviction disclosure, and CME certification (50 hours per 2-year cycle per the board's CME rule).

faqs.question: What happens if I miss my expiration date?
faqs.answer: MD: your status flips to Delinquent immediately; within 30 days you owe a 10 percent delinquent fee, and past 90 days an additional 50 percent penalty fee, on top of the $1,206 renewal. faqs.question: What does the status 'Valid to Practice While Reviewed' mean?

faqs.question: Does Indiana require CME to renew?

faqs.question: I'm retiring. Do I still need to renew?

faqs.question: When does my Iowa medical license expire and how often do I renew?

faqs.question: My license went inactive. How do I get it back?

faqs.question: Do MDs and DOs renew with the same board?

faqs.question: How much does renewal cost?

faqs.question: Do I need malpractice insurance to hold an active Kansas license?

faqs.answer: Late renewal begins August 1. You must submit a late renewal request through MELS with an explanation, and the Board must approve it; you are notified by email once approved. Fines are a $25 base fine plus $5 for each month the license remains delinquent.

faqs.question: My license has been expired for more than a year. Can I still renew?

faqs.question: Does the 8-hour DEA opioid training count toward Mississippi requirements?

faqs.question: How often do I renew my New Hampshire physician license, and when is it due?
faqs.answer: Every 2 years. Under RSA 310:8 your license is valid for 2 years from its date of issuance, and the completed renewal application, fee, and any supporting documents must be filed on or before the license expiration date. OPLC sends an email renewal notification 90 days before expiration and is required by statute to notify you at least 2 months before expiration.

faqs.question: How much does renewal cost?
faqs.answer: $413.00 for a Physician or Administrative Physician license (Compact Physician renewal is also $413.00), per the OPLC Board of Medicine fee page. This includes the mandatory $28.00 Professional Health Program (PHP) fee. Online payment accepts Mastercard, Visa, Discover, and American Express.

faqs.question: Where do I renew?
faqs.answer: Through the New Hampshire Online Licensing system at https://forms.nh.gov/license/Login.aspx, via the OPLC Customer Portal. First-time online renewers create an account using the registration code printed on their renewal notification; if you need a code, email CustomerSupport@oplc.nh.gov with your name, telephone number, and license number.

faqs.question: What happens if I miss my renewal deadline?
faqs.answer: Your license expires and you are not authorized to practice until it is reinstated; there is no grace period or late-renewal path (RSA 310:8, III). Physician reinstatement costs $413.00 ($378.00 for Compact Physicians). One year after expiration the license lapses, after which you cannot renew and must reinstate by submitting an application and meeting the eligibility requirements in statute and board rules.

faqs.question: Do I have to do anything besides the renewal application and fee?

Physicians renewing an active-status license must complete the NH Physician Licensure Survey or the opt-out form through DHHS, required by RSA 126-A:5, XVIII-a (administrative and inactive licenses are exempt). Your CME (100 hours per 2-year cycle, at least 40 Category 1, plus 3 hours in pain management/addiction disorders for NH-DEA holders) is now tracked through CE Broker, which OPLC made mandatory for the Board of Medicine as of February 3, 2025.

faqs.question: I hold my NH license through the Interstate Medical Licensure Compact. Is my renewal different?
faqs.answer: The board posts a separate document, Important Information for Compact Physician License Renewals, linked from the Applications for Physician page, and the fee schedule lists Compact Physician as its own category (renewal $413.00, reinstatement $378.00). Review that document before renewing rather than assuming the standard path applies.

Reinstatement (N.J.S.A. 45:1-7.4; request application via BMEReinstatement@dca.njoag.gov) requires: renewal application, certification of employment for every job held during suspension, the current biennial renewal fee, the unpaid back renewal fee, a $175 reinstatement fee, and proof of the CME that was due (board presentation adds a criminal history background check). The new 2-credit sexual misconduct prevention CME (N.J.A.C. 13:35-6.15(e), adopted May 2025) must be completed before the close of the renewal in 2027 and must cover all seven board-specified topics; a single generic harassment course may not qualify (board alert on njconsumeraffairs.gov/bme).

Reduced-fee ($125) retired-active renewal for physicians 65+ still carries the FULL 100-credit CME requirement, and CME applies whether or not you actually practice in New Jersey; only no-fee Inactive or Retired status (no practice, no prescribing) is CME-exempt (board FAQ).

Reinstatement after a renewal lapse is expensive and slow: current cycle fee plus the unpaid back-cycle renewal fee plus $175 reinstatement fee plus $100 late fee, a new criminal history background check, CME verification, and a job-by-job employment certification for the whole suspension period.

faqs.question: When does my New Jersey medical license expire?
faqs.answer: On June 30 of odd-numbered years, for every MD and DO regardless of issue date. The current biennial period ends June 30, 2027. The board mails a renewal notice at least 60 days before expiration.

faqs.question: How much does renewal cost?
faqs.answer: $580 for an active MD/DO license ($290 per year of the biennial period). Physicians 65 or older with no HMO or hospital affiliation may renew as reduced-fee active-retired for $125. Renewing as Inactive or Retired is free, but those statuses bar practicing and prescribing in New Jersey.

faqs.question: What happens if I miss the June 30 deadline?
faqs.answer: You have a 30-day statutory window: renew with the $580 renewal fee plus a $100 late fee, and your license stays valid during those 30 days. After 30 days the license is suspended automatically without a hearing, and continuing to practice is unlicensed practice even if you never got a notice.

faqs.question: How do I get reinstated after my license was suspended for non-renewal?
faqs.answer: Request a reinstatement application by emailing BMEReinstatement@dca.njoag.gov. You must submit the renewal application, a certification listing every job held during the suspension, the current cycle's renewal fee, the unpaid back renewal fee, a $175 reinstatement fee, proof of the required CME, and complete a criminal history background check. Holding a current license in good standing in another state, with that state's CE met, satisfies the CME piece.

faqs.question: Do DOs renew through a different board?
faqs.answer: No. New Jersey has one board: the State Board of Medical Examiners licenses both MDs and DOs (and podiatrists) on the same June 30 odd-year cycle, and the board's FAQ confirms DOs hold all the same practice authority as MDs.

faqs.question: Do I have to finish my CME before renewing?
faqs.answer: Yes. 100 credits (at least 40 Category 1) for the two years before renewal is a condition of biennial renewal, including the topic mandates such as the 2-credit sexual misconduct prevention course due before the close of the 2027 renewal. Waiver or extension requests must be sent by certified mail at least 60 days before expiration; hours are never prorated for mid-cycle licensure unless you qualify for the new-graduate initial-cycle exemption.

states.boardName: New Mexico Medical Board
states.renewalAnchor: On or before July 1 of every third year (NMSA 1978 Section 61-6-26). Licenses expire July 1; online renewal must be completed by June 30. Renewal opens about 3 months before expiration. Initial licenses are issued for no more than 13 months and no less than 1 month, expiring the following July 1, which places the new licensee into the triennial cycle.

After 2 years: reinstatement application, 75 hrs CME for the past 3 licensing years, fees, possible current-competency exam (16.10.3.11 NMAC) and board interview (16.10.7.17). Board FAQ adds a $200 penalty for lapsed-for-non-renewal versus having chosen another status by June 30. DO reinstatement fee is $500 (16.17.2.8(C)(4) NMAC).

Log in to the New Mexico Medical Board renewal portal
Complete the renewal application and answer the attestation questions
Pay the renewal fee ($600 total (active physician triennial renewal: $450 renewal fee plus $150 impaired physicians program fee, 16)
Submit and save your confirmation
pitfalls: October 1 is the real cliff: the license stays temporarily valid for practice through September 30 with late fees, then on October 1 it is lapsed for non-renewal, and the board notifies New Mexico hospitals and health insurance plans (16.10.7.9 NMAC).

Renewal triggers a one-time fingerprint-based nationwide and statewide criminal history screening; renewals can be granted while the state screening is pending, but a missing background check will hold up issuance (16.10.7.9(A) NMAC and board FAQ).

Missing the 75-hour CME requirement by October 1 automatically lapses the license, and the board FAQ warns you will be audited on the next cycle and cannot reuse those same late-earned hours even though they fall inside the next renewal window.

Not receiving a renewal notice is no defense: NMSA 61-6-26(A) and 16.10.7.10 NMAC put address accuracy on the licensee, and since November 14, 2019 the board assesses a $150 administrative cost for failing to update your address.

DO logistics diverge slightly from MD despite the merged board: the osteopathic rule chapter (16.17 NMAC) sets late fees of $200 (July 2 to September 29) and $400 (after September 29) and a $500 reinstatement fee, versus the MD $100/$200 late fees and $400 reinstatement.

Retired status is a one-way door: a retired NM license may not be reinstated; you must re-apply as a new applicant (16.10.7.13(B) NMAC). Voluntary lapsed or inactive status preserves the cheaper reinstatement path.

faqs.question: When exactly is my New Mexico renewal due?
faqs.answer: On or before July 1 of every third year (NMSA 61-6-26). The board says to complete online renewal no later than June 30; the portal opens about 3 months before expiration. Your specific due year depends on when you were first licensed, since initial licenses are dated to expire the following July 1.

faqs.question: How much does renewal cost?
faqs.answer: $600 for an active physician license: $450 triennial renewal plus a $150 impaired physicians program fee (16.10.9.8(B) NMAC). Telemedicine licenses renew triennially for $400. Placing a license on inactive status costs a one-time $25 processing fee.

faqs.question: What if I miss July 1?
faqs.answer: You can still practice: the license remains temporarily active until September 30. Renewing by August 15 adds a $100 late fee; August 16 through October 1 adds $200. If you have not renewed by October 1, the board may suspend the license for non-renewal and mark it lapsed, and NM hospitals and health plans are notified (16.10.7.9, 16.10.7.14, 16.10.9.8 NMAC).

faqs.question: How do I get a lapsed license back?
faqs.answer: Within 2 years of the renewal date: written reinstatement request, renewal application, proof of required CME, and the renewal fee plus a $400 reinstatement fee ($200 if you were on inactive status). After 2 years: reinstatement application, 75 hours of CME for the past 3 licensing years, fees, and possibly a current-competency exam and board interview (16.10.7.16 to 16.10.7.18 NMAC).

faqs.question: I am a DO. Do I renew with a separate osteopathic board?
faqs.answer: No. The Board of Osteopathic Medicine was merged into the New Mexico Medical Board (all statutory references transferred June 18, 2021; the old board was repealed effective July 1, 2022), and DOs renew through the same NMMB portal. The osteopathic rule chapter (16.17 NMAC) is still on the books with a $600 triennial renewal, slightly different late fees ($200 July 2 to September 29, $400 after), and DO-specific CME (75 hrs with a 30-hour AOA Category 1-A/1-B minimum).

faqs.question: Do I need fingerprints or a background check to renew?
faqs.answer: Yes, once. All renewal applications are subject to a one-time nationwide and statewide fingerprint-based criminal history screening (16.10.7.9(A) NMAC). The renewal can be processed and even granted while the statewide screening is pending, but the board FAQ says a completed background check is needed to issue or renew any license.

faqs.question: How fast do I get my renewed license?
faqs.answer: Issued and mailed within 5 working days after you renew, per the board FAQ; longer if you answered Yes to any professional practice question. You can also print an unofficial copy from your portal account.

states.renewalCycle: Biennial (2 years) registration; the license itself is valid for life
states.renewalAnchor: Rolling per-licensee registration period: NY Education Law 6502 has the Department establish the beginning date of each licensee's registration period, so the two-year cycle runs from your own registration date, not a birth month or fixed statewide date. NYSED mails a Registration Renewal Document with a PIN approximately four months before the registration expires (per the Office of the Professions FAQ). Physicians and medical physicists are on two-year periods; most other NY professions are three-year.

states.graceOrLapse: There is no grace period to practice: practicing after a lapse requires actual possession of the registration certificate, and failure to register while practicing can be deemed professional misconduct. Online renewal remains available until 4 months after the registration period ends; after that you must submit a paper Delayed Registration Application, paying the $600 plus $10/month late fees. Paying a delayed registration re-registers you for the full lapsed period in question, not a fresh two years from the payment date. Physicians not practicing in NY can switch to Inactive status free of charge and avoid late fees; resuming practice requires re-registration and any applicable post-licensure requirements.
states.processingTime: Online renewals: up to 2 business days (longer if the renewal requires review); address changes 2 business days; optional professional photo ID card about 6 weeks
steps: Complete your CME for the cycle (0 hours)
Log in to the New York State Education Department, Office of the Professions (State Board for Medicine) renewal portal
Complete the renewal application and answer the attestation questions
Pay the renewal fee ($600 (registration renewal for Medicine, MD and DO, per two-year registration period; Office of the Professions Fees Chart, Rev)
Submit and save your confirmation
pitfalls: Your NY medical license never expires, but your registration does, every 2 years. Physicians (and medical physicists) are the exception to New York's usual 3-year professional registration cycle, so physicians who also hold another NY professional license will have mismatched cycles.

Online renewal requires the seven-character PIN from the Registration Renewal Document NYSED mails about four months before expiration. If your address on file is stale you will not get the notice; the PIN can be retrieved at https://eservices.nysed.gov/professions/renewal/retrieve-pin.

Practicing with a lapsed registration is not a paperwork technicality: Education Law bars resuming practice without actual possession of the registration certificate, and failure to register while practicing can be charged as professional misconduct. If you are not practicing in NY, file for free Inactive status instead of ignoring the notice.

faqs.question: Does my New York medical license expire?
faqs.answer: No. Under Education Law 6502 the license is valid for the life of the holder unless revoked, annulled, or suspended. What expires is your registration to practice, which physicians must renew every two years with NYSED's Office of the Professions.

faqs.question: How much does renewal cost?
faqs.answer: $600 per two-year registration period for Medicine (MD and DO), per the Office of the Professions Fees Chart. Online payment is by credit card only (Visa, MasterCard, American Express) and fees are not refundable. An optional professional photo ID card is an extra $30.

faqs.question: How do I renew online?
faqs.answer: Use the NYSED eServices portal at https://eservices.nysed.gov/professions/renewal/start with the seven-character PIN from the Registration Renewal Document mailed to you about four months before expiration. You can renew online if no more than 5 months remain in your current period or your last period ended less than 4 months ago. Processing takes up to 2 business days.

faqs.question: What happens if I miss my renewal?
faqs.answer: A late filing fee of $10 accrues for each month registration is delayed. Within 4 months of expiration you can still renew online; after that you must submit a Delayed Registration Application. Payment re-registers you for the full lapsed period, not a new two years, and you cannot practice until you actually possess the registration certificate.

faqs.question: Is there a CME requirement to renew?
faqs.answer: New York has no general CME hour requirement for physician registration renewal. Separate mandates still apply: infection control coursework every four years, a one-time child abuse identification course, and the NYS mandatory prescriber education (3 hours pain management, palliative care, and addiction) for DEA-registered prescribers under NYSDOH rules.

faqs.question: I am not practicing in New York right now. Do I still have to pay?
faqs.answer: No. You can place your registration in Inactive status free of charge and owe no late fees for the inactive period. To resume practice you must re-register and meet any post-licensure requirements for the profession before practicing.

faqs.question: When is my North Carolina medical license renewal due?
faqs.answer: Every year, no later than 30 days after your birthday, regardless of when your license was issued. This applies to both MDs and DOs, and your first renewal is due within 30 days of your next birthday even if it falls soon after issuance.

faqs.question: How much does renewal cost?
faqs.answer: $250 per year for MDs and DOs, paid by credit card through the Licensee Gateway at portal.ncmedboard.org. A $50 late fee is added if you renew more than 30 days after your birthday.

faqs.question: What happens if I miss the deadline entirely?
faqs.answer: Thirty days after your birthday the $50 late fee attaches and the board sends a certified letter giving you a final 30 days. If you still have not renewed, your license automatically goes inactive and it is unlawful to practice on it.

faqs.question: How do I get my license back after it goes inactive?

Out of clinical practice 2+ years may also trigger a case-by-case competence assessment.

faqs.question: Is the renewal processed right away?

faqs.answer: Renewal is online only at www.pals.pa.gov; there are no paper renewal applications. Renewals open approximately 60 days before the expiration date, and PALS emails you when your renewal is available. The boards also mail notices 2 to 3 months before expiration.

faqs.question: How much does renewal cost?
faqs.answer: $360 for an unrestricted MD license and $450 for an unrestricted DO license, each covering the 2-year cycle. IMLC compact licensees pay an additional $25.00 IMLC renewal fee through imlcc.com.

faqs.question: What happens if I miss the deadline?

The online renewal window opens in early May (May 6 in 2026) and closes promptly at 4:30 pm EDT on June 30; unrenewed licenses expire at 11:59 pm EDT on June 30. DO: license is valid for a term of 2 years and must be renewed by June 30 of the second year (W. Va. Code R. 24-1-4); the statute states renewal is biennial on or before July 1 (W. Va. Code 30-14-10), and the DO board requires the application and fees by June 30.
states.cmeDetails: MD: 50 hours per 2-year cycle. at least 50 Category 1, 3 hrs controlled substances. DO: 32 hours per 2-year cycle. at least 16 Category 1, 3 hrs controlled substances.
states.renewalFee: $400 (MD active status, 2-year renewal; inactive status is $150). DO renewal is also $400.00 plus a 2.25% processing fee when paying by credit card.
states.lateFee: No late fee as such for MDs: there is no late-renewal option. The license expires at 11:59 pm EDT June 30 and the physician must instead apply for reinstatement at $600 for an active status license. DO board: no late fee published on the pages loaded; failure to renew triggers automatic suspension under W. Va. Code 30-14-10, and reinstatement requires back fees plus a reinstatement fee set by board rule (amount not verified).
states.graceOrLapse: None. The MD board states: "Because there is no grace period for practice after expiration, the Board strongly encourages early renewal" and "You may not practice medicine or surgery, write prescriptions or administer prescription drugs in West Virginia with an expired license under any circumstances." An expired MD may apply for reinstatement ($600 active) during the 12 months after expiration (July 1 through June 30 of the following year); applications are processed in order received, cannot be expedited, and any discrepant application waits for the next Licensure Committee meeting. The physician cannot practice until reinstatement is approved. For DOs, failure to renew operates as an automatic suspension of the license (W. Va. Code 30-14-10); restoration requires proof of CME for the prior two years, payment of all accumulated biennial fees, and a reinstatement fee per board rule.
states.processingTime: Most MD renewal applications are processed within three business days (2026 Renewal FAQ). DO processing time not published on pages loaded.
steps: Complete your CME for the cycle (50 hours) (see details below)
Log in to the West Virginia Board of Medicine renewal portal
Complete the renewal application and answer the attestation questions
Pay the renewal fee ($400 (MD active status, 2-year renewal; inactive status is $150))
Submit and save your confirmation
pitfalls: The portal closes before your license does: MD online renewal ends promptly at 4:30 pm EDT on June 30 even though the license itself is valid until 11:59 pm that night. Miss the 4:30 cutoff and your only path is a $600 reinstatement with committee-review delays.

Your renewal year depends on your last name, not your license issue date: A through L renew in even years (e.g. 2026), M through Z in odd years (e.g. 2025). Physicians who change names or move from another state routinely misjudge their cycle.

CME must be finished before you submit: the Board answers "Can I renew my license in May and finish up my CME after I renew?" with a flat "No." You are not eligible to renew until all 50 hours (and the 3-hour controlled substance course, if you prescribed) are complete, and you are subject to random CME audit.

CSMP registration is a separate renewal trap: if you prescribed or dispensed any Schedule II-V controlled substance under your WV license, you must hold and maintain access to the Board of Pharmacy's CSMP database before renewing. Your DEA registration does not count.

Renewal is online only, credit card only, and personal: no paper option, no other payment method, a personal (non-delegate) email address is required, only the physician may complete the renewal, and the Board warns against using phones or tablets for the process. Delegating renewal to office staff is explicitly not authorized.

faqs.question: When does my West Virginia MD license expire?
faqs.answer: At 11:59 pm EDT on June 30 of your renewal year: even-numbered years if your last name begins with A through L, odd-numbered years if it begins with M through Z. The online renewal window opens in early May and closes at 4:30 pm EDT on June 30.

faqs.question: How much does renewal cost?
faqs.answer: $400 for an active status MD license, $150 for inactive status, paid online by credit card only. DOs pay $400 plus a 2.25% credit card processing fee to the separate Board of Osteopathic Medicine.

faqs.question: What happens if I miss the deadline?
faqs.answer: Your license expires and there is no grace period; you may not practice, prescribe, or administer prescription drugs on an expired license under any circumstances. You may apply for reinstatement ($600 active) during the 12 months after expiration, but you cannot practice until it is approved, applications cannot be expedited, and discrepant applications wait for Licensure Committee review.

faqs.question: Do I have to finish my CME before I renew?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Board states you are not eligible to renew until all required CME for the two-year cycle is complete, including the 3-hour Board-approved controlled substance prescribing course if you prescribed controlled substances in WV during the cycle. No documents are uploaded at renewal, but keep records for the random CME audit.

faqs.question: Can my office manager renew for me?
faqs.answer: No. The Board states you are the only person authorized to renew your license, and it requires a personal email address that is not a delegate account. Login uses your last name, WVBOM license number, and the last four digits of your SSN.

faqs.question: I am a DO. Is my renewal different?
faqs.answer: Yes, entirely. DOs renew through the separate West Virginia Board of Osteopathic Medicine: a 2-year license renewed by June 30 of the second year (your expiration year is on your license, not tied to your last name), $400 plus 2.25% card processing fee, via the D.O. Dashboard at wvbdosteo.org. CME is 32 hours per cycle (16 AOA Category 1) plus the 3-hour drug diversion course.

states.name: Wisconsin
states.boardName: Wisconsin Medical Examining Board (Department of Safety and Professional Services, DSPS)
states.doBoardName: null-equivalent: none. Wisconsin has no separate osteopathic board; the Medical Examining Board licenses both MDs and DOs (the DSPS physician page covers "medical and osteopathic physicians," and the fee schedule lists Medicine and Surgery (MD) and Medicine and Surgery (DO) as parallel credentials of the same board).
states.renewalAnchor: October 31 of each odd-numbered year, for all physicians statewide (Wis. Stat. 440.08(2)). The board states this applies even if the initial license was issued in the months just before the date: a license issued shortly before October 31 of an odd year still must be renewed by that date. Next renewal deadline: October 31, 2027.
states.cmeDetails: 30 hours per 2-year cycle. at least 30 Category 1, 2 hrs opioid prescribing.
states.renewalFee: $120 (Medicine and Surgery, MD or DO, 2-year renewal). Same $120 applies to the Compact (IMLC-issued) MD and DO credentials and to Administrative Medicine and Surgery licenses. Per the DSPS Renewal Dates and Fees schedule (RDAF, rev. 08/07/2025); DSPS's August 8, 2025 news release confirms the physician fee rose to $120 effective for applications opening in August 2025.
states.lateFee: $25 late renewal fee, making the total $145 with the renewal fee (Wis. Stat. 440.08(3)(a); RDAF schedule shows $145 "with late fee" for MD and DO).
states.graceOrLapse: No practice grace period: the license expires October 31 if no renewal was filed. However, under Wis. Stat. 227.51(2) (quoted on the DSPS physician page), if the renewal application and fee are submitted by 11:59 pm on the deadline, the existing license remains valid until DSPS finishes acting on the application. After expiration, the credential can be restored at any time by paying the renewal fee plus the $25 late fee (Wis. Stat. 440.08(3)(a)). If expired more than 5 years, the board may impose additional restoration requirements to establish competency, not to exceed initial-licensure education/exam requirements (Wis. Stat. 440.08(3)(b)). DSPS may also summarily deny a renewal to protect public health, safety, or welfare, with a 30-day window to request a hearing (Wis. Stat. 440.08(4)).
states.processingTime: DSPS does not publish a physician renewal processing time on its site. The board page notes that a timely-filed renewal keeps the license valid while under review (Wis. Stat. 227.51(2)), and employers can confirm active status via DSPS Public Look-Up. At a September 30, 2025 DSPS renewal webinar (reported by the Wisconsin Hospital Association), DSPS said legal file reviews take about one week once all requested information is received.
steps: Complete your CME for the cycle (30 hours) (see details below)
Log in to the Wisconsin Medical Examining Board (Department of Safety and Professional Services, DSPS) renewal portal
Complete the renewal application and answer the attestation questions
Pay the renewal fee ($120 (Medicine and Surgery, MD or DO, 2-year renewal))
Submit and save your confirmation
pitfalls: The renewal date is fixed at October 31 of odd years no matter when the license was issued. DSPS states explicitly that a physician first licensed in the months leading up to the date must still renew by that date, so a new licensee can owe a full renewal within weeks of initial licensure.

IMLC (Interstate Medical Licensure Compact) licensees do not renew through the Wisconsin LicensE portal; DSPS directs them to renew at imlcc.com/renew. Renewing in the wrong system stalls the renewal.

Renewal holds tied to the Office of the Commissioner of Insurance (typically Injured Patients and Families Compensation Fund compliance) blocked some 2025 renewals; DSPS addressed these at its September 30, 2025 webinar. Resolve any OCI/fund issue before the October 31 deadline rather than waiting for DSPS to clear it.

For the 2025 cycle, CME was attested at renewal, not uploaded: DSPS said CE Broker would not be used for the renewal itself but would be used for post-renewal audits. Physicians must retain CME completion evidence through the biennium because the Medical Examining Board runs random audits (Wis. Admin. Code MED ch. 13).

The renewal addendum (Form 4570) asks health, substance use, discipline, DEA, and malpractice-payout questions scoped to what has 'not been previously disclosed.' A yes answer, or an incomplete addendum, routes the file to legal review and delays the renewal, so gather supporting documentation before starting.

faqs.question: When is my Wisconsin medical license renewal due?
faqs.answer: October 31 of every odd-numbered year, for every MD and DO regardless of when the license was first issued (Wis. Stat. 440.08(2); DSPS physician page). The next deadline is October 31, 2027.

faqs.question: How much does renewal cost?
faqs.answer: $120 for the 2-year renewal for both MDs and DOs, per the DSPS Renewal Dates and Fees schedule (rev. 08/07/2025). DSPS raised the fee to $120 in August 2025 and notes it remains the lowest physician renewal fee in the nation.

faqs.question: Where do I renew?
faqs.answer: Online through the LicensE portal at license.wi.gov (log in, My Approved Licenses, choose Renew from the Action dropdown). Physicians licensed through the Interstate Medical Licensure Compact renew at imlcc.com/renew instead. A paper route exists via the Medicine and Surgery Renewal Addendum, Form 4570.

faqs.question: Can I keep practicing if DSPS has not finished processing my renewal by November 1?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you submitted the application and paid the fee by 11:59 pm on October 31. Under Wis. Stat. 227.51(2), a timely and sufficient renewal keeps the existing license valid until DSPS finally acts on it. You must stay responsive to any DSPS requests, and your employer can verify status on DSPS Public Look-Up; DSPS will not issue written confirmation.

faqs.question: What happens if I miss the deadline?
faqs.answer: The license expires and you cannot practice on it, but you can restore it by paying the $120 renewal fee plus a $25 late fee ($145 total) under Wis. Stat. 440.08(3)(a). If the license has been expired more than 5 years, the board may require additional competency-related requirements before restoring it (Wis. Stat. 440.08(3)(b)).

faqs.question: What CME do I need to attest at renewal?
faqs.answer: 30 hours of Category 1 CME (AMA, AOA, or ACCME-approved) per biennium, including 2 hours on prescribing opioids and other controlled substances for physicians holding a DEA number (Wis. Admin. Code MED ch. 13). You attest at renewal and keep proof for the board's random post-renewal audits; for the 2025 cycle DSPS said CE Broker is used for audits, not for the renewal itself.

states.name: Wyoming
states.boardName: Wyoming Board of Medicine
states.renewalAnchor: Fixed date: all physician licenses must be renewed no later than June 30 of each calendar year, and each renewal carries the license through the next June 30 (Board rule, Ch. 1 Sec. 10; W.S. 33-26-305 requires annual lapse on a board-set date). First-time renewal depends on issue date: licenses issued July 1 through February 28/29 renew by the immediately following June 30; licenses issued March 1 through June 30 renew by June 30 of the next calendar year.
states.cmeDetails: 60 hours per 3-year cycle. at least 60 Category 1, 1 hrs controlled substances.
states.cmeSource: WY Board of Medicine Rules Ch. 3, § 7
states.renewalFee: $155 (annual physician renewal, incl. administrative license, per Board fee schedule PDF effective January 30, 2023). EXCEPTION: the Board entirely waived the renewal fee for the 2026-2027 renewal year during its software conversion; paper renewals still pay a $25 paper processing fee. IMLC-issued licenses renewed via IMLCC paid $0 to Wyoming this year plus the IMLCC $25 processing fee.
states.lateFee: $100 license renewal grace period surcharge (fee schedule PDF). During the current 2026 grace period the Board quotes $125 total for paper renewal: $100 surcharge plus $25 paper processing fee.
states.graceOrLapse: 90-day grace period: a physician who misses June 30 may still renew by submitting the renewal application, renewal fee, and $100 grace period surcharge no later than September 30 (Board rule Ch. 1 Sec. 10). For 2026 the Board states all grace period renewals and fees must be RECEIVED in the Board office by 5:00 p.m. on September 30, 2026, and grace period renewal is by paper form. After the grace period the license lapses. Reactivation of a lapsed license (rule Ch. 1 Sec. 12) requires a board application, applicable fees ($250 reactivation per fee schedule, which covers an NPDB report, criminal record check if necessary, and license through the next June 30), two references, and proof of at least 60 hours of qualified CME within the preceding 3 years; the Board may require a licensure interview, and without one reactivation requires a majority vote of the Board. Reinstatement is a separate $300 pathway on the fee schedule, and costs may also be imposed under Ch. 4 Sec. 3(k).
states.processingTime: Up to 7 business days after completing the 2026-2027 online renewal form for it to be fully processed and a license mailed (Board's own renewal page, June 2026). No published processing time for paper or grace period renewals.
steps: Complete your CME for the cycle (60 hours) (see details below)
Log in to the Wyoming Board of Medicine renewal portal
Complete the renewal application and answer the attestation questions
Pay the renewal fee ($155 (annual physician renewal, incl)
Submit and save your confirmation
pitfalls: Wyoming renews EVERY year on June 30, not biennially. The CME reporting cycle is 3 years, which misleads physicians into assuming a multi-year license; the license itself lapses annually (W.S. 33-26-305; Board rule Ch. 1 Sec. 10).

The 2026-2027 renewal window is already CLOSED (it ended 5:00 p.m. June 30, 2026). Until September 30, 2026 the only path is the paper grace period renewal mailed to the Board office with $125 ($100 surcharge + $25 paper processing fee), and it must be RECEIVED, not postmarked, by 5:00 p.m. September 30, 2026.

The Board is mid software conversion: the 2026-2027 renewal ran on a Google Docs form linked from the Board's renewal page, and the old GLSuite portal page (wybomv7prod.glsuite.us) now says all 2026 physician renewals are done by paper. Do not hunt for the legacy online login.

Physicians licensed via the IMLC (Wyoming license number ends in the letter C) cannot renew on the Board's form alone: they must renew through https://imlcc.com/renew/ first, after which Board staff email a link to a required Board renewal form. Both steps are required.
The renewal fee waiver is a one-time 2026-2027 event tied to the software conversion. The standing fee is $155 per year, all fees are non-refundable, and paper filings always add $25.

If the license lapses after September 30, reactivation is not a formality: $250 fee, two references, proof of 60 hours of CME within the preceding 3 years, a new NPDB report, and possibly a licensure interview or a majority vote of the Board.

faqs.question: When does my Wyoming physician license expire?
faqs.answer: June 30 of every calendar year. All physician licenses (other than temporary and training licenses) lapse annually, and every renewal carries the license through the next June 30. First-time renewal timing depends on when the license was issued: issued July 1 to February 28/29, renew by the immediately following June 30; issued March 1 to June 30, renew by June 30 of the next calendar year.

faqs.question: How much does renewal cost?
faqs.answer: The standing fee is $155 per year (Board fee schedule effective 1-30-2023), plus $25 if you renew on a paper form. For the 2026-2027 renewal year only, the Board entirely waived the renewal fee while it converts software systems; paper renewals still owed the $25 processing fee.

faqs.question: I missed the June 30 deadline. Can I still renew?
faqs.answer: Yes, during a 90-day grace period ending September 30, with a $100 grace period surcharge added to the renewal fee. For 2026, grace period renewal is by paper form only ($125 total: $100 surcharge plus $25 paper fee) and must be received in the Board office no later than 5:00 p.m. on September 30, 2026.

faqs.question: What happens if I miss the September 30 grace deadline?
faqs.answer: The license lapses and you must apply for reactivation: a Board application, the $250 reactivation fee (covers an NPDB report and criminal record check if necessary), two references, and proof of at least 60 hours of qualified CME completed within the preceding 3 years. The Board may require a licensure interview; without one, reactivation requires a majority vote of the Board.

faqs.question: My Wyoming license came through the Interstate Medical Licensure Compact. Do I renew differently?
faqs.answer: Yes. If your license number ends in the letter C, you must renew directly through the IMLCC website (https://imlcc.com/renew/). Wyoming's fee this year is $0 and the IMLCC charges a $25 processing fee. After the IMLCC notifies the Board, Board staff email you a link to complete a required Board renewal form. Both steps are required.

faqs.question: How do I renew online, and how long does processing take?
faqs.answer: Start at the Board's Renew License page (https://wyomedboard.wyo.gov/physicians/renew-license). Because the Board is converting software systems, the 2026-2027 renewal used a Google Docs form linked from that page rather than the old online portal. The Board states it may take up to 7 business days after completing the form for the renewal to be fully processed and a license mailed.
